newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude trades again at Oct +15 cts, Med firms.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude trades again at Oct +15 cts, Med firms.

text.p: A cargo of Brent crude oil was bought by a refiner on Tuesday at October Brent +15 cents - repeating Monday's traded level, sources said.
The September 15-17 loading Brent, taken by a trader as a late pass after being five o' clocked on Monday, sold on late Tuesday to a U.K. refiner.
A Sept 16-18 Brent also moved at the same level.

The wet North Sea market was still struggling with sellers lowering their offers on middle decade September cargoes. The Brent/WTI spread, which has come in some 10-15 cents since Friday, did little to support a sagging market, traders said.

Two of Tuesday's cargoes from the paper chains were kept by British Petroleum and expected to be offered on the market on Wednesday, traders said. Shell Trading (Stasco) was five o' clocked with the third.
Talk of a September 16-18 Oseberg trading at Dated Brent +32 cents could not be immediately confirmed but sources saw some cheaper cargoes on offer around those dates.

October Brent traded at $21.75 by 1730 GMT, down some 24 cents on the day. Intermonth spreads came off with the fall in outright levels to +60/65 cts for Sep/Oct, +65/70 cents for Oct/Nov and +61/65 cents for Nov/Dec.
Spot crudes in the Mediterranean were firmer on the indefinite postponement of the resumption of Iraqi exports and loading delays at the Russian port of Novorossiisk.
"With the Novorossiisk programme delayed and the Iraqi news everything's looking a lot firmer," said a trader.

Regional benchmark sour Russian Urals, which traded last Thursday at Dated Brent -$1.03 a barrel, was sold for 90 cents a barrel below the bell-wether crude on Monday. Other barrels loading Sept 10-15 were offered at -80 cents on Tuesday.
Syrian Light sellers also benefitted from the improved sentiment, reporting two firm bids for September barrels.
